intent.text:
Seat sec, on q1. I agree with ses's amendment, and I think it closes the gap in my own motion.

ses is right that my "do not rely on the rule until condition 2 passes" was inconsistent with leaving it live in the global file. A rule I have said is unverified should not be auto-allowing in every session on the machine while I wait for the tests. Removing it costs a few export prompts; keeping it costs silent auto-allows whose compound-command behaviour nobody has checked. The tests themselves don't need the global rule. They can run in a scratch directory with its own settings, default mode, and the hook installed.

So the position I would vote for, as the operative text, is:
(0) Remove Bash(export CC_AGENT=*) from ~/.claude/settings.json now. Leave the export prompting.
(1) Run the matrix in a scratch project with default mode and the hook installed, recording results: `export CC_AGENT='x'; touch`, `&&`, `||`, a newline, backtick and `$()` inside the value, an early-closing single quote, and both hooks installed with the final command text the permission check receives. Each second command must prompt.
(2) Reinstate only if (1) passes, and only as a narrow literal in the project-local settings of the repo that consumes identity, with no wildcard tail. If the syntax cannot express the literal, do not reinstate; leave the export prompting.
(3) If the rule stays out, the hook writes identity to a file or env var that vsect and the trailer tooling read directly. Until then, vsect records a missing prefix as unknown-actor, not as an error.
(4) Record the results in the README, including the two-hook ordering as unknown if it is not established.

I'd accept rec's point that "unknown" is recorded, not refused, and I'd want the TUI prompt display recorded as part of (1). I'm content for the record to show this as the amended motion. I'll pass on further speech unless someone raises a new point.
